proposals.hypothesis: Li6Si2O7 is a Li-rich, wide-gap silicate. Si4+ is hard to reduce, so the framework should resist reaction with the sulfide electrolyte, and the oxide should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li. Its Li fraction (about 0.4 per atom) is higher than that of most available phosphates and borates, which should keep the penalty per non-Li atom low.
proposals.motivation: Earlier Li8SiO6 proposal pointed to Li-rich orthosilicates with Si4+ frameworks as the target. Li6Si2O7 is the available Li-rich silicate closest to that concept.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-ion conductor that is widely used as a cathode coating. Its oxidative stability extends to about 4 V, and it is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte, so it should give a small interfacial penalty at the 4.0 V setpoint.

LiF is a very wide-gap (about 7 eV), electronically insulating Li-ion-conducting fluoride. It is oxidatively robust near 4 V versus Li, so it should not be oxidized by LiCoO2. It is also chemically compatible with the sulfide electrolyte, since the fluoride anion is hard to oxidize and the Li-F interface is thermodynamically quite stable. These properties suggest a small interfacial penalty at the 4.0 V setpoint.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluation of the Li3PO4 phosphate (mp-aaaaaegs) established a wide-gap, insulating Li-rich oxide baseline. LiF extends that search to a different anion family (halide) with a larger gap and higher oxidative stability.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich binary oxide. It is thermodynamically stable against the sulfide electrolyte and is oxidatively robust at 4 V vs Li, so it should give a small interfacial penalty at the 4.0 V setpoint. It also belongs to a different family (other_oxide) from the earlier phosphate and halide choices.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluations of Li3PO4 and LiF established that wide-gap, Li-rich, electrochemically robust insulators are the target. Li2O is the simplest member of that class and is not yet explored.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating orthoborate. Its Li content and oxidative stability near 4 V vs Li should suit a LiCoO2 interlayer, and it offers a different anion family (borate) from the phosphate, halide, and oxide classes already proposed. This is an exploratory choice with an unverified sulfide-compatibility assumption.

Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating silicate. Al3+ and Si4+ are hard to reduce, so the framework should resist reaction with the sulfide electrolyte. Its oxidative stability near 4 V vs Li should keep it from being oxidized by LiCoO2. The silicate family has not been explored yet, so this is a new-family test.
